# Skelcrew

> Skelcrew is open source software that runs a small crew of coding agents on tasks, in parallel and unattended, with a human as the team lead. Tasks go in; branches, pull requests or reports come out.

Status: in active development. The rebuild started on 8 October 2026 and has not had a public release yet. Updates: https://skelcrew.dev/#updates

## How it works

- A task is the unit of work, not a chat. Add one with `skel add "<description>"` (GitHub issues and trackers are planned).
- A planner agent triages it: intent (quick fix, bug, investigation, feature, exploration, prototype) and how much care it needs.
- A builder agent does the work in its own git worktree.
- A separate tester agent reviews it adversarially and collects evidence, for up to three rounds.
- Changes to paths marked critical wait for the human's sign-off. The result is a branch, a pull request or a report.
- When an agent needs the human, it asks a short question with options instead of chatting.

## Guarantees

- A small deterministic core enforces the rules; agents only propose.
- No agent can approve its own work, ship without review, or start more agents than allowed.
- The commit that passed review is exactly the commit that is delivered.
- Every step is an event in an append-only log that can be replayed.
- Work is saved before an agent stops, and a crash or restart resumes where it left off.

## Compatibility

- Harnesses: Claude Code today; Codex next. Others through plugins.
- Runs in the terminal on a laptop or an always-on machine. Uses git and GitHub.
- Bring your own AI subscription. The core is free and open source. A hosted control plane at skelcrew.dev is planned.

## Configuration example (skelcrew.yaml)

```yaml
roles:
  planner: { harness: claude }
  builder: { harness: claude }
  tester:  { harness: codex }
repo:
  test: [bun run check]
  critical: [src/core/**]
limits:
  max_running: 2
```
